asr_text: The researchers also erased a way to throw rocks to get more blocks from one AI's memory. After that, the average number of towers it could build went down. Its scores on other tasks stayed the same. For this AI, at least, remembering that way helped it build towers. One tip in the strategy notes was worth paying attention to. Even so, it is too soon to wave a flag and say, play and get smarter, proof complete. The experienced group did better, and removing one memory lowered its score. These two results need to be studied separately. By themselves, they do not show that play itself made a difference. Still, this changes how we think about a detour. A discovery that is not useful now might be a useful card to play next time, if it is saved. If you see an AI jumping around on the island, watch its notes as well as its feet. Its next tower might depend on a discovery written down in just one line.
